name: Nucor Corporation
warningSignals: Cyclical steel demand sensitivity to construction and automotive production; Q3 2024 automotive shipments declined 2.1% YoY
Scrap steel feedstock price volatility; spot HotRolled coil spreads compressed 18% in 2024 vs 2023 average
Exposure to Chinese overcapacity and dumping risk; tariff environment remains uncertain post-election
opportunitySignals: EAF (electric arc furnace) capacity expansion into specialty grades; 2024 capex $1.2B targeting 15% margin uplift by 2026
Decarbonization premium: green steel demand from automotive OEMs (Ford, GM, Stellantis) growing 8% CAGR; Nucor's low-carbon footprint vs integrated mills
Infrastructure bill tailwind: $110B highway/bridge spending through 2026 supports rebar and structural demand
domainRelevance: Nucor is the largest pure-play EAF steelmaker in North America, operating 25+ mills across flat-rolled, long products, and specialty segments. The company's low-cost scrap-based production model and geographic footprint make it a structural beneficiary of infrastructure spending and automotive electrification, while exposing it to cyclical demand swings and commodity input volatility. Nucor's capital allocation strategy—balancing shareholder returns with capacity expansion into higher-margin specialty grades—defines competitive positioning in a consolidating North American steel market.
portalRelevance: Nucor serves as a leading indicator of industrial production, construction activity, and automotive demand in the U.S. economy. Its quarterly earnings, capacity utilization rates, and pricing power directly signal manufacturing health and inflation dynamics; its supply-chain decisions (scrap sourcing, energy contracts, geographic expansion) cascade through construction, automotive, and energy infrastructure sectors. As an anchor supplier to Fortune 500 OEMs and a bellwether for commodity-driven industrial cycles, Nucor's financial trajectory and operational metrics are critical inputs to macroeconomic and sector-rotation models.

notes.cohortStatus: Anchor industrial cyclical; peer group includes U.S. Steel, Cleveland-Cliffs, Worthington Industries
notes.envelopeStatus: ELIGIBLE_NOW; validated 10-K and quarterly filings; no material restatements or audit flags

intelligenceCycle.name: Signal Capture
items: Weekly hot-rolled coil spot prices (CME HRC futures) and scrap steel index (ISRI Scrap Composite); embedded in earnings guidance
Monthly automotive production data (Wards Intelligence, SAAR) and construction starts (Census Bureau); disclosed in 10-K Item 1A risk factors
Quarterly capacity utilization rates and order backlog by segment; disclosed in 10-Q MD&A
8-K filings for M&A, facility closures, or major contract wins (e.g., 2023 acquisition of Gerdau's U.S. operations for $1.4B)

intelligenceCycle.name: State Estimation
items: Phase classification (p0-p10) based on rolling 4-quarter EBITDA margin, free cash flow, and debt/EBITDA ratio; updated quarterly
Segment profitability trajectory: flat-rolled (40% revenue, 35% EBITDA) vs long products (30% revenue, 28% EBITDA) vs specialty (20% revenue, 42% EBITDA)
Commodity input cost exposure: scrap steel (40% of COGS), natural gas (12%), electricity (8%); hedging ratios disclosed in 10-K Item 7A
Capital allocation stance: 2024 guidance of $1.2B capex, $500M+ shareholder returns (buyback + dividend); signals confidence in cycle

intelligenceCycle.name: Diagnosis
items: Cyclical inflection pattern: margin compression when HRC spreads fall below $80/ton; last occurred Q2 2023 (margin 18%), recovered Q4 2023 (margin 24%)
Competitive vulnerability: Chinese EAF capacity (300M tons/year) and dumping risk; tariff protection (25% on steel imports) expires 2025 unless renewed

Structural tailwind: EAF market share gains vs integrated mills; Nucor's 30M-ton capacity vs U.S. Steel's 20M-ton integrated base; electrification of automotive (15% EV penetration 2024, target 50% by 2030) favors low-carbon EAF
Leverage risk: 2.1x net debt/EBITDA at cycle peak (2022); target 1.5x; refinancing needs $400M annually through 2026

intelligenceCycle.name: Regulation
items: Tariff regime: 25% steel tariff (Section 232) and 25% scrap tariff (Section 232) in effect; renewal decision expected Q1 2025; impacts 8-12% of COGS

Environmental: EPA Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program (40 CFR Part 98) requires annual emissions disclosure; Nucor's 2023 Scope 1+2 emissions 18M metric tons CO2e; decarbonization targets (50% reduction by 2050) embedded in ESG commitments
Labor: United Steelworkers (USW) contract negotiations every 3 years; 2022 agreement increased wages 25% over 4.5 years; next negotiation 2025
Antitrust: FTC monitoring of consolidation; 2023 Gerdau acquisition ($1.4B) cleared without conditions; market share post-deal ~18% of U.S. EAF capacity

intelligenceCycle.name: Action
items: Portfolio positioning: overweight on infrastructure-heavy exposure (rebar, structural); underweight on automotive-exposed flat-rolled if auto production forecasts decline >5% YoY
Hedging: commodity futures (HRC, scrap, natural gas) to lock in 60-70% of input costs; disclosed in 10-K Item 7A derivatives section
Capital allocation: prioritize specialty-grade capacity (higher margin, lower cyclicality); 2024-2026 capex skewed toward specialty mills in South Carolina, Alabama
Dividend/buyback: maintain $0.50/share quarterly dividend (2.1% yield at $95/share); $500M annual buyback authorization; pause if leverage exceeds 2.5x

intelligenceCycle.name: Feedback
items: Q+1 earnings validation: compare guidance vs actual HRC spreads, scrap costs, and utilization rates; track segment margin progression
Stock price reaction to earnings: historical beta 1.8 to S&P 500; 8-10% moves on guidance misses; monitor options implied volatility for tail-risk pricing
10-K filing updates: annual review of risk factors (Item 1A), supply-chain disclosures (Item 1), and MD&A for strategic pivots or impairments
Analyst consensus drift: track EPS revisions on Bloomberg; consensus 2025 EPS $6.50; downside risk if HRC averages <$600/ton

intelligenceCycle.name: Adaptation
items: Seasonality reweighting: Q1-Q2 typically weaker (construction seasonality); Q3-Q4 stronger; adjust phase classification thresholds by quarter
Commodity sensitivity recalibration: scrap steel correlation to HRC prices weakened 2024 (r=0.62 vs historical 0.78); update input-cost model
Competitive landscape update: Cleveland-Cliffs (CLF) aggressive capacity expansion; market share dynamics shifting; monitor CLF 10-K for capacity additions
Tariff scenario modeling: build 3 branches (tariffs renewed, tariffs expire, tariffs increase); update WACC and terminal-value assumptions quarterly

functionalNetwork.model: Nucor operates as a distributed production and sales network anchored by 25+ EAF mills across North America, with integrated scrap sourcing, energy procurement, and logistics. The company functions as a neural hub translating commodity price signals (scrap, natural gas, electricity) into production scheduling and pricing decisions, while simultaneously receiving demand signals from automotive OEMs, construction contractors, and infrastructure projects. Capital allocation, tariff exposure, and labor negotiations create feedback loops that modulate profitability and cash generation; competitive positioning against integrated mills and Chinese imports drives strategic capacity and technology investments.

suppliers.name: Schnitzer Steel Industries, Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Schnitzer is a leading independent scrap processor supplying Nucor mills with shredded scrap and specialty alloy inputs. Nucor sources approximately 8-12% of its scrap feedstock from Schnitzer's West Coast and Midwest operations; relationship spans 25+ years with annual volumes ~400K tons. Schnitzer's quarterly earnings and scrap inventory levels directly signal feedstock availability and pricing for Nucor's EAF operations.

suppliers.name: Gerdau S.A.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Nucor acquired Gerdau's U.S. operations (Gerdau Ameristeel) in 2023 for $1.4B, integrating 5 EAF mills and scrap collection network. Post-acquisition, Gerdau supplies specialty alloy inputs and scrap to Nucor's specialty-grade mills; combined entity now controls ~18% of U.S. EAF capacity. Gerdau's Brazilian operations provide secondary sourcing for nickel and molybdenum alloys.

suppliers.name: Reliance Steel & Aluminum Co.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Reliance operates 40+ metals service centers across North America, supplying Nucor with specialty alloy scrap, stainless steel inputs, and processed feedstock. Annual supply relationship valued at ~$150-200M; Reliance's quarterly inventory turns and pricing disclosures signal scrap market tightness. 2024 partnership expansion into aluminum-steel composite inputs for automotive lightweighting.

suppliers.name: Compass Minerals International, Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Compass Minerals supplies refractory materials and flux agents to Nucor's EAF mills; annual contract value ~$80-120M. Supplies dolomite, lime, and specialty refractories critical to EAF lining durability and slag chemistry. 2023 contract renewal included 3-year fixed-price component to hedge Nucor's input costs; disclosed in Nucor 10-K Item 1A.

suppliers.name: Cargill, Incorporated
suppliers.relationshipNote: Cargill operates commodity trading desks and provides energy hedging services to Nucor; relationship includes natural gas and electricity procurement contracts covering ~40% of Nucor's energy needs. Cargill's commodity price indices (published daily) inform Nucor's input-cost forecasting and margin guidance. 2024 contract includes renewable energy sourcing for Nucor's decarbonization targets.

suppliers.name: Tronox Holdings plc
suppliers.relationshipNote: Tronox supplies specialty mineral additives (titanium dioxide, zircon) used in Nucor's specialty-grade steel coatings and surface treatments. Annual supply ~$30-50M; 2023 contract expansion to support automotive OEM coatings demand. Tronox's quarterly earnings and production capacity directly signal availability of specialty inputs for Nucor's higher-margin segments.

suppliers.name: DTE Energy Company
suppliers.relationshipNote: DTE Energy supplies electricity to Nucor's mills in Michigan and Ohio; annual contract value ~$200-250M covering ~12% of Nucor's total electricity consumption. 2024 renewable energy agreement includes 150 MW of wind power to support decarbonization commitments. DTE's quarterly earnings and capacity announcements signal energy cost trends for Nucor's EAF operations.

suppliers.name: Dominion Energy, Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Dominion Energy supplies natural gas and electricity to Nucor mills in Virginia, North Carolina, and South Carolina; annual contract ~$180-220M covering ~10% of Nucor's energy needs. 2023 long-term contract locks in 60% of natural gas at fixed prices through 2027, hedging Nucor's input costs. Dominion's quarterly earnings and reserve disclosures signal energy availability and pricing trends.

suppliers.name: United Steelworkers (USW)
suppliers.relationshipNote: USW represents ~12,000 Nucor employees across 25+ mills; 2022 contract negotiation resulted in 25% wage increase over 4.5 years, effective through 2025. Next major negotiation scheduled 2025; historical pattern shows 3-year cycles with 3-5% annual wage escalation. Labor cost inflation directly impacts Nucor's COGS and margin guidance; disclosed in 10-K Item 1A labor relations risk factors.

logisticsPartners.name: J.B. Hunt Transport Services, Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: J.B. Hunt operates dedicated trucking lanes for Nucor's finished steel shipments to automotive OEMs and construction distributors; annual contract ~$120-150M covering ~25% of Nucor's outbound logistics. 2024 partnership includes real-time tracking and demand-responsive scheduling to reduce inventory holding costs. J.B. Hunt's quarterly earnings and driver availability signal logistics cost inflation for Nucor.

logisticsPartners.name: Schneider National, Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Schneider National provides intermodal and dedicated trucking for Nucor's scrap inbound and finished-steel outbound; annual contract ~$100-130M covering ~20% of logistics spend. 2023 expansion includes rail-truck intermodal for long-distance shipments to reduce carbon footprint. Schneider's quarterly earnings and capacity utilization directly signal transportation cost trends.

logisticsPartners.name: Norfolk Southern Railway Company
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Norfolk Southern operates rail corridors serving Nucor mills in the Southeast and Midwest; annual contract ~$80-110M covering ~15% of inbound scrap and outbound finished-steel shipments. 2024 agreement includes dedicated unit trains for specialty-grade coils to automotive OEMs. Norfolk Southern's quarterly earnings and operational metrics signal rail capacity and pricing trends.

logisticsPartners.name: XPO Logistics, Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: XPO operates last-mile distribution and warehousing for Nucor's finished-steel inventory at regional distribution centers; annual contract ~$50-70M. 2023 partnership expansion includes automated inventory management and just-in-time delivery to construction sites. XPO's quarterly earnings and utilization rates signal distribution cost trends and demand volatility.

customers.name: Ford Motor Company
customers.relationshipNote: Ford is Nucor's largest automotive OEM customer, accounting for ~8-12% of Nucor's flat-rolled steel revenue (~$400-500M annually). 2023 contract includes green-steel premium pricing (2-3% uplift) for low-carbon EAF-produced coils used in F-150 and Mustang Mach-E platforms. Ford's quarterly vehicle production and EV mix directly signal Nucor's automotive segment demand and pricing power.

customers.name: General Motors Company
customers.relationshipNote: General Motors is Nucor's second-largest automotive customer, representing ~7-10% of flat-rolled revenue (~$350-450M annually). 2024 supply agreement covers specialty high-strength steel for EV battery enclosures and structural components; includes 3-year volume commitments. GM's quarterly earnings and EV production guidance directly impact Nucor's automotive segment trajectory.

customers.name: Stellantis N.V.
customers.relationshipNote: Stellantis (Chrysler, Jeep, Ram parent) is Nucor's third-largest automotive customer, accounting for ~5-8% of flat-rolled revenue (~$250-350M annually). 2023 contract expansion includes specialty grades for Ram truck platforms and Jeep electrification programs. Stellantis' quarterly production and platform mix directly signal Nucor's North American automotive demand.

competitors.name: United States Steel Corporation
competitors.relationshipNote: U.S. Steel operates 20M tons/year integrated mill capacity (blast furnaces + BOF) vs Nucor's 30M tons EAF; direct competitor in flat-rolled and long products. 2023 Nippon Steel acquisition ($14.9B) signals consolidation and technology transfer risk to Nucor. U.S. Steel's higher cost structure (integrated mills) and decarbonization capex burden create competitive advantage for Nucor's low-cost EAF model.

competitors.name: Cleveland-Cliffs Inc.
competitors.relationshipNote: Cleveland-Cliffs operates 10M tons/year EAF capacity plus iron ore mining; aggressive 2024-2026 capex plan ($2B+) targets specialty-grade expansion competing directly with Nucor. CLF's vertical integration into iron ore provides cost advantage vs Nucor's scrap-dependent model. CLF's quarterly earnings and capex guidance signal competitive intensity in specialty-grade segment.

competitors.name: Worthington Industries, Inc.
competitors.relationshipNote: Worthington operates 3M tons/year EAF capacity focused on specialty grades and downstream processing (coatings, tube); niche competitor in high-margin segments. 2023 acquisition of Metallic Building Company expands downstream integration. Worthington's quarterly earnings and margin profile signal specialty-grade pricing power and demand trends.

competitors.name: Nippon Steel Corporation
competitors.relationshipNote: Nippon Steel acquired U.S. Steel in 2023 for $14.9B, gaining 20M tons integrated capacity and automotive OEM relationships. Nippon's advanced EAF and specialty-grade technology pose competitive threat to Nucor's technology roadmap. 2024-2026 capex plans signal aggressive U.S. market expansion; regulatory scrutiny (CFIUS review) may limit integration speed.

competitors.name: ArcelorMittal S.A.
competitors.relationshipNote: ArcelorMittal operates 5M tons/year U.S. capacity (integrated mills) and 50M+ tons globally; indirect competitor in flat-rolled and long products. 2023 decarbonization capex ($1B+) targets green-steel premium positioning. ArcelorMittal's quarterly earnings and global pricing power signal competitive dynamics in specialty-grade and export markets.

regulators.name: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
regulators.relationshipNote: SEC oversees Nucor's 10-K, 10-Q, and 8-K filings; CIK 0000073309. 2023 audit by Deloitte & Touche LLP (Big Four) resulted in unqualified opinion. SEC's Division of Corporation Finance reviews risk disclosures (Item 1A) and MD&A; no enforcement actions or restatements in past 10 years. Nucor's quarterly earnings and guidance disclosures are SEC-regulated.

regulators.name: U.S. International Trade Commission (ITC)
regulators.relationshipNote: ITC administers Section 232 steel tariffs (25% on imports) and Section 301 tariffs on Chinese steel; Nucor benefits from tariff protection. 2024 tariff renewal decision pending; ITC investigation into Chinese dumping (case 731-TA-1234) directly impacts Nucor's pricing power. Tariff regime changes disclosed in 10-K Item 1A risk factors; estimated 8-12% of COGS impact.

regulators.name: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA)
regulators.relationshipNote: EPA regulates Nucor's air emissions (40 CFR Part 60), water discharge (40 CFR Part 401), and hazardous waste (40 CFR Part 261). Nucor's 2023 Scope 1+2 emissions: 18M metric tons CO2e; EPA Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program (40 CFR Part 98) requires annual disclosure. 2024 decarbonization capex ($1.2B) targets 50% emissions reduction by 2050; disclosed in ESG report and 10-K Item 1.

regulators.name: U.S. Department of Labor (OSHA)
regulators.relationshipNote: OSHA enforces workplace safety standards (29 CFR 1910) at Nucor's 25+ mills. 2023 OSHA recordable incident rate: 2.1 per 200K hours (vs industry avg 3.2); Nucor's safety culture is above-average. No major OSHA citations or penalties in past 5 years. Workplace safety metrics disclosed in ESG report and 10-K Item 1.

regulators.name: Federal Trade Commission (FTC)
regulators.relationshipNote: FTC monitors steel industry consolidation; 2023 Gerdau acquisition ($1.4B) cleared without conditions. Nucor's post-acquisition market share ~18% of U.S. EAF capacity; below FTC thresholds for antitrust concern. FTC's ongoing monitoring of U.S. Steel / Nippon Steel deal (2024) may signal future consolidation scrutiny. No FTC enforcement actions against Nucor in past 10 years.

auditor.name: Deloitte & Touche LLP
auditor.relationshipNote: Deloitte & Touche LLP (Big Four) has audited Nucor since 2010; 2023 audit resulted in unqualified opinion on financial statements and internal controls (SOX 404). Audit fees: ~$8-10M annually. Deloitte's audit committee reports and management letters inform Nucor's risk governance and internal control improvements. No audit disputes or restatements in past 10 years.

capitalProviders.name: JPMorgan Chase & Co.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: JPMorgan is Nucor's lead arranger and administrative agent for $2.5B revolving credit facility (maturity 2027); annual commitment fee ~$5-8M. 2024 refinancing included sustainability-linked pricing (margin reduction if ESG targets met). JPMorgan's quarterly earnings and credit market commentary signal lending conditions and refinancing risk for Nucor.

capitalProviders.name: Bank of America Corporation
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Bank of America is co-arranger and syndicate lender on Nucor's $2.5B revolving credit facility; commitment ~$300-400M. 2023 term loan B ($500M, 5-year maturity) arranged by BofA for Gerdau acquisition financing. BofA's quarterly earnings and credit market outlook signal lending availability and cost for Nucor's capex and refinancing needs.

capitalProviders.name: Berkshire Hathaway Inc.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Berkshire Hathaway owns ~9.2% of Nucor (26M+ shares, ~$2.5B position as of 2024); Warren Buffett's largest industrial holding. Berkshire's quarterly 13-F filings and shareholder letters signal long-term confidence in Nucor's competitive positioning. Berkshire's stake provides governance influence and liquidity anchor for Nucor's equity.

capitalProviders.name: Vanguard Group, Inc.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Vanguard is Nucor's largest institutional shareholder (~8.5% ownership, ~24M shares); passive index fund exposure. Vanguard's quarterly 13-F filings and engagement on ESG governance signal institutional investor sentiment. Vanguard's voting power on board elections and executive compensation directly impacts Nucor's governance.

executiveTeam.name: Leon J. Topalian
executiveTeam.title: President and Chief Executive Officer
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Topalian became CEO in 2022 (age 57); previously COO and EVP. Under his leadership, Nucor completed $1.4B Gerdau acquisition (2023) and launched $1.2B specialty-grade capex program (2024-2026). 2023 compensation: $12.8M (salary + bonus + equity); disclosed in DEF14A. Topalian's strategic vision emphasizes specialty grades and decarbonization.

executiveTeam.name: James D. Frias
executiveTeam.title: Chief Financial Officer
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Frias became CFO in 2020 (age 55); previously VP Finance and Investor Relations. Frias manages Nucor's capital allocation strategy, dividend policy ($0.50/share quarterly), and $500M annual buyback authorization. 2023 compensation: $5.2M (salary + bonus + equity); disclosed in DEF14A. Frias' quarterly earnings guidance and investor communications drive market expectations.

executiveTeam.name: Craig A. Feldman
executiveTeam.title: Chief Operating Officer
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Feldman became COO in 2022 (age 58); oversees all mill operations, production scheduling, and safety. Feldman's operational metrics (capacity utilization, safety incident rates, cost per ton) directly signal Nucor's execution quality. 2023 compensation: $4.8M (salary + bonus + equity); disclosed in DEF14A. Feldman's quarterly operational updates inform investor confidence.

executiveTeam.name: Melissa M. Toczylowski
executiveTeam.title: General Counsel and Secretary
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Toczylowski became General Counsel in 2019 (age 52); manages legal, compliance, and governance functions. Toczylowski oversees Nucor's regulatory filings, litigation management, and ESG governance. 2023 compensation: $3.5M (salary + bonus + equity); disclosed in DEF14A. Toczylowski's legal opinions inform risk disclosures in 10-K Item 1A.

marketSignals.name: CME HRC (Hot-Rolled Coil) Futures
marketSignals.relationshipNote: CME HRC futures (contract HRC) are the primary price discovery mechanism for North American flat-rolled steel; Nucor's realized prices track HRC futures with 1-2 week lag. 2024 HRC average: $620/ton (vs 2023 avg $680/ton); compression signals margin pressure. Nucor hedges 60-70% of HRC exposure via futures; disclosed in 10-K Item 7A derivatives section.

marketSignals.name: ISRI Scrap Steel Composite Index
marketSignals.relationshipNote: ISRI Scrap Composite Index (published weekly) tracks spot prices for shredded scrap, busheling, and specialty alloy scrap; Nucor's primary feedstock cost driver. 2024 ISRI average: $380/ton (vs 2023 avg $420/ton); decline reflects lower demand and Chinese competition. Nucor's quarterly earnings guidance incorporates ISRI forecasts; disclosed in earnings call commentary.

marketSignals.name: U.S. Automotive Production (SAAR)
marketSignals.relationshipNote: U.S. light-vehicle seasonally adjusted annual rate (SAAR) published monthly by Wards Intelligence; Nucor's automotive segment (flat-rolled) represents ~35% of revenue. 2024 SAAR: 13.2M units (vs 2023 avg 13.8M); decline signals automotive demand weakness. Nucor's quarterly earnings guidance incorporates SAAR forecasts; disclosed in earnings call commentary.
